principle: Do not accept a link only because its source and target appear at similar order positions. Confirm with local evidence, reverse-order evidence, and relation cues.

algorithms.name: monotonic_global_sequence_assignment
algorithms.use_when: Most commentary explains paadal phrases in the same order.
constraints: Allow skip source and skip target states.
Use gap penalty for unmatched spans.
Use relation cue score as pair emission score.
algorithms.formula: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j-1] + pair_score(i,j) + order_bonus, dp[i-1][j] - source_gap_penalty, dp[i][j-1] - target_gap_penalty)

algorithms.name: reverse_order_alignment
algorithms.recommended_method: run the same DP once forward and once with target sequence reversed
algorithms.use_when: Commentary explains a line in reverse or summary-first order.
algorithms.decision: If reverse_score > forward_score + margin, allow reverse mapping and mark sequence_alignment_method='reverse_order'.

algorithms.name: neighboring_span_constraints
algorithms.use_when: A row has weak evidence but previous/next accepted links are strong.
constraints: If previous source maps to target k and next source maps to target k+2, current source should prefer target k+1.
Penalize targets far outside the previous-next window.
Boost candidate if it shares entity or relation family with neighbor row.

algorithms.name: relation_cue_confirmation
algorithms.use_when: Order score is high but lexical score is low.
algorithms.rule: Do not upgrade confidence unless relation cue score >= threshold.

scoring_update.old_issue: order_score can dominate even when semantic support is absent
scoring_update.new_rule: order_score alone cannot raise confidence above low
